origins.section: The Harness Reruns One Snapshot in Fresh Processes
It Fails Loudly, and the Failure Points at the Cause
A Determinism Test Belongs in the Test Suite

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-processes: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-processes: A loop that solves the same model five times in one Python process hides two of the sources above: every solve shares one hash salt, so a set has the same order each time, and HiGHS keeps the thread count its first solve chose. (README_10.2.1.md, Design Note)
recorded.prompt:q-diagnosis: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-diagnosis: "The status and objective are not in the list, so every run proved the same value; only the plan and the work differ. Same value, different plan: a tie picked differently, here by the build order." Table row: "result.plan, plan_digest, perhaps stats; not objective | a tie, picked by order, seed or version".
recorded.prompt:q-known-bad: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-known-bad: Design note: "A determinism test that has never failed proves nothing about its own strength: it might compare the wrong field, or run everything in one process. That is why harness.py and the module's tests include configs that are known not to repeat, and assert that they fail."

recorded.prompt:q-processes:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-processes:a: `hash()` and the set's order change with the salt; `sorted()` and a SHA-256 digest from `hashlib` do not, because they depend only on the characters. (README_10.2.1.md)
recorded.prompt:q-processes:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-processes:c: Wall time is not in the manifest (lesson 10.2.4 keeps `wall_seconds` apart), so the clock never enters the comparison. (README_10.2.5.md)
recorded.prompt:q-processes:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-processes:d: The salt is set by the environment variable `PYTHONHASHSEED`: unset or `random` means a new salt per process; an integer fixes it; `0` turns the salting off. (README_10.2.1.md)
recorded.prompt:q-diagnosis:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-diagnosis:a: Table: "inputs.* | the runs did not read the same snapshot or options". The manifest records inputs.snapshot, so a changed snapshot would list inputs.snapshot, and the message does not.
recorded.prompt:q-diagnosis:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-diagnosis:b: Table: "versions.* | different software: an unpinned environment". The manifest records versions.ortools, so another version would appear as versions.ortools in the message, and it does not.
recorded.prompt:q-diagnosis:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-diagnosis:c: Table: "result.stats only, or more, under a time limit | the clock". 10.2.4: "A clock-limited run that happened to return the same plan still shows different iteration counts". This message lists no result.stats.
recorded.prompt:q-known-bad:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-known-bad:b: The known-bad configs are a model-building bug ("lesson 10.2.1's bug, the count question built from a set's order") and expected racing ("points to threads racing"), not solver bugs. The stated purpose is "so the test suite also proves the harness can fail".
recorded.prompt:q-known-bad:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-known-bad:c: "check stops at the first run that differs from run 1, so it counts nothing: a config passes or it fails."
recorded.prompt:q-known-bad:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-known-bad:d: check compares each config's runs only with that config's own run 1 ("compares every manifest with the first"), never with another config's digest. The stated purpose is to show the harness can fail.
